cleanIntro: The HP-15 is Hi-Point's AR-pattern rifle and pistol, in 5.56x45 and .300 BLK, and one book covers every configuration with one procedure. It strips the AR way: two takedown pins, the upper lifts off the lower, the bolt carrier and charging handle slide out the back, and the book goes on to take the bolt out of the carrier. It has nothing in common with Hi-Point's blowback pistols and carbines — no slide retainer pin, no punch and hammer — and, like the carbines, it has no magazine disconnect, so it will fire with the magazine out. Work in the printed order; the book says the order is what proves the rifle empty.

steps.title: Magazine out — the HP-15 has NO magazine disconnect
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger outside the trigger guard. Press the magazine release button on the right side of the lower receiver, just above and forward of the trigger guard, and pull the magazine clear. Removing it does nothing to the trigger: a round in the chamber still fires with the magazine on the bench. Take every loose round off the bench before going on.
steps.prose: Unload all magazines and get live ammunition out of the area first — the book asks for that before disassembly begins.
steps.quote: 1. Remove the magazine by depressing the magazine release button. (FIG. 1)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 1, p.23
steps.warn: Your Hi-Point HP-15 does not have a magazine disconnect and will still fire with the magazine removed.

steps.title: Selector to SAFE — it will not go there with the hammer down
steps.action: Rotate the selector on the left of the lower receiver to SAFE. If it will not turn, the hammer is already down: the HP-15's safety cannot be engaged on a released hammer, and it only moves to SAFE once the charging handle has been pulled and the hammer re-cocked. Do not force the lever; pull the charging handle in the next step and come back to it.
steps.prose: On SAFE a cam bears on the rear of the trigger and blocks the hammer from being released.
steps.quote: 2. Rotate the thumb safety to the safe position. Note: If the hammer has been released the safety will not engage to the fire position (FIG. 2)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 2, p.23

steps.title: Charging handle fully back to throw out a chambered round
steps.action: Hold the pistol grip in your right hand, finger off the trigger and outside the guard, ejection port facing away from you. With your other hand pull the charging handle fully to the rear to extract and eject anything in the chamber. A round that falls clear is still live; set it apart from the empties.
steps.quote: 3. While holding the grip with your right hand, with your finger off of the trigger and outside of the trigger guard, grasp the operating/charging handle with your other hand and pull the operating/charging handle fully back to eject any cartridge that may be in the chamber. (FIG. 3)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 3, p.24

steps.title: Lock the bolt open on the bolt release
steps.action: Hold the magazine well with your left hand and pull the charging handle to the rear with your right, then press the BOTTOM of the bolt release with your left hand so the bolt catch rises and holds the bolt open. Ease the charging handle forward and check the bolt stays back.
steps.prose: The disassembly chapter's own step 4 describes locking the bolt with a charging-handle roller and a receiver shroud slot, parts the HP-15's parts list does not contain. The method above is the one this book gives in its Unloading chapter.
steps.quote: 4. Lock the breech bolt in the rearward (open) position by Hold the mag well with your left hand, with your right pull the charging handle to the rear, then with your left hand press the bottom of the bolt release in to lock the bolt in the open position. (Fig.4)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 7, Unloading, step 4, p.22

steps.title: Look AND feel — chamber and magazine well
steps.action: With the bolt locked back, look into the chamber through the ejection port and into the magazine well, then put a fingertip into both. The last-round hold-open is not the check and neither is your memory; on a black rifle a fingertip is what settles a dark chamber.
steps.quote: 5. Once the breech bolt is locked to the rear, visually and physically (with your finger) inspect the chamber and the magazine well of your Hi-Point HP-15 to be sure that no ammunition remains in either place. (FIG. 5)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 5, p.24
steps.warn: Although your Hi-Point HP-15 has a last round hold open, never rely on it to determine whether your Hi-Point HP-15 is unloaded.

steps.title: Bolt forward on the bolt release
steps.action: Only once you are sure the rifle is empty, press the bolt release button and let the bolt run forward to the closed position. The receivers are separated with the bolt home.
steps.quote: Once you are sure your Hi-Point HP-15 is unloaded, release the bolt by depressing the bolt release button. (FIG. 5.1)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 5, p.24

steps.title: Rear takedown pin pushed across
steps.action: Find the rear takedown pin at the back of the receivers, under the forward assist, and push it across with a fingertip or a small punch until the upper is free at the rear. The book only asks you to push it in, not to pull it out; its parts list carries a takedown pin detent and spring for it in the lower.
steps.quote: 6. Using your finger or a small punch too, depress the rear take down pin under the forward assist. (FIG. 6)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 6, p.24

steps.title: Front takedown pin across, upper lifted off
steps.action: Push the front takedown pin, above the magazine well, across the same way, then pull the upper receiver upward and lift it clear of the lower. From now until the rifle is back together, keep your finger off the trigger: with the upper gone there is nothing to stop the hammer.
steps.prose: Set the lower down with the hammer cocked and leave it that way.
steps.quote: Using your finger or a small punch too, depress the front take down pin above the mag well. (FIG. 6.1) Pull upward on the upper receiver and lift it off. (FIG. 6.2)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 6, p.25
steps.warn: Do not pull the trigger with out the upper receiver attached. The hammer can damage the lower receiver when released under full spring tension and could crack the lower receiver.

steps.title: Charging handle back, bolt carrier out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle to the rear; it brings the bolt carrier assembly with it, and the carrier slides out of the back of the upper receiver. The charging handle stays in the upper for now.
steps.quote: 7. Pull the charging handle to the rear and remove the bolt carrier assembly. (FIG. 7)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 7, p.25

steps.title: Charging handle back to the keyway and down out
steps.action: Draw the charging handle further back until its lugs reach the keyway in the upper receiver, then drop it down and out. It only leaves at that one point; if it will not drop, it is not far enough back.
steps.prose: Note the ears on the front of the handle — they line up with the notch in the upper when it goes back in.
steps.quote: 8. Remove the charging handle by pulling it backwards to keyway and down out of the upper receiver. (FIG. 8)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 8, p.25

steps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out, right to left
steps.action: On the bolt carrier, push the firing pin retaining pin through from the RIGHT side to the left and take it out. It is a small cotter-style pin and easily lost, so do this over the bench.
steps.prose: It goes back in the opposite way, left to right.
steps.quote: 9. Push in the firing pin retaining pin from right to left of the bolt carrier (FIG.9 and FIG.10) and remove the pin.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 9, p.25

steps.title: Bolt face up, firing pin slides out the back
steps.action: Tilt the carrier so the bolt face points up and let the firing pin slide out of the rear of the carrier. Catch it; do not shake the carrier to get it moving.
steps.quote: 10. Tilt the bolt face up and remove the firing pin from the bolt carrier group. (FIG. 11)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 10, p.26

steps.title: Bolt pushed in, cam pin turned 90 degrees
steps.action: Push the bolt face back toward the carrier until the bolt rotates and stops. Then turn the bolt cam pin a quarter turn, 90 degrees from where it sat. If it will not turn, push the bolt in until it has rotated and stopped.
steps.prose: The book numbers these steps 10, 12 and 13 — there is no printed step 11, and nothing is missing between them.
steps.quote: 12. To Push in on the bolt face towards the carrier until the bolt rotates and comes to a stop, then rotate the bolt cam pin 90 degrees from its original position. (FIG. 12)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 12, p.26

steps.title: Cam pin lifted out, bolt drawn forward out of the carrier
steps.action: Lift the cam pin up and out of the bolt and carrier, then pull the bolt forward and out of the front of the carrier. That is the last step of the book's disassembly; the extractor, ejector and gas rings stay on the bolt.
steps.quote: 13. Remove the bolt cam pin by lifting it out and away from the bolt and bolt carrier group (BCG) (FIG.13). Pull the bolt forward and out of the bolt carrier group (BCG) (FIG. 13.1)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 8, Disassembly, step 13, p.26

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber end, rod through the upper
steps.action: With the bolt carrier out, the chamber is open at the back of the upper. Run a solvent-wet patch through the barrel from the chamber end several times on a cleaning rod, then a solvent-wet bristle brush back and forth from the same end, then an oiled patch, repeating brush and patch until the patch comes out clean. Finish the outside of the barrel with a nylon brush and wipe it dry.
steps.prose: Before firing, run clean dry patches from the chamber end until no oil comes out — unless the rifle is going into storage.
steps.quote: 1. Wet a cleaning patch with a gun cleaning solvent or a cleaner-lubricantpreservative and run it through the barrel, from the chamber end, several times using a cleaning rod.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Complete Cleaning, Barrel, step 1, p.27

steps.title: Jacketed ammunition only
steps.action: While the bore is in front of you, know what it may be fed. Hi-Point restricts the HP-15 to jacketed ammunition to stop lead building up in the barrel, and to commercially made ammunition meeting SAAMI, CIP or NATO standards. Lead fouling is one of the things the inspection at the end of this clean looks for.
steps.quote: Only use jacketed ammunition to prevent the buildup of lead deposits in the barrel.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 4, Loading, p.14
steps.warn: Use of improper ammunition could cause death or serious personal injury and/or property damage. Only use high quality commercially manufactured ammunition that meets SAAMI, CIP or NATO standards.

steps.title: Carrier inside and out, cam pin area, rails
steps.action: Lubricate the bolt carrier on its inner and outer surfaces, the area around the cam pin, and the rails where the carrier rides on the inside of the upper receiver. Then the bolt itself: the cam pin area and the gas rings, with only a light touch on the extractor and its pin. A light coat on the firing pin, and lubricate the charging handle with its latch and spring.
steps.quote: 2. Bolt Carrier: Lubricate the inner and outer surfaces of the bolt carrier. Lubricate the cam pin area and the BCG rail areas where it makes contact with the inside of the upper receiver.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Complete Cleaning, Bolt Carrier Group, step 2, p.28

steps.title: Carrier key dried, then ONE drop of CLP
steps.action: The carrier key on top of the carrier takes the gas. Dry its inside with a cotton swab or pipe cleaner, then put a single drop of CLP inside — one drop, not a squirt.
steps.quote: 5. Carrier Key: The inside of the carrier key on the bolt should be dried with cotton swab or pipe cleaner - then place one drop of CLP inside.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Complete Cleaning, Bolt Carrier Group, step 5, p.28

steps.title: Lower receiver lubricated in place
steps.action: The lower is cleaned and oiled assembled — the book takes nothing out of it. Lubricate every moving part you can reach: trigger, hammer, safety, bolt catch and magazine release, with their pins and detents, plus the takedown pins and their detents. Lightly oil the buffer and buffer spring where they sit inside the buffer tube, and wipe fingerprints off the outside with a lint-free cloth.
steps.prose: Upper side: lightly oil the inside of the upper, around the barrel's locking lugs and the forward assist, and check the forward assist works.
steps.quote: 5. Lower Receiver: Lubricate all moving parts inside the lower including the trigger, hammer, safety, bolt catch, magazine release, and their corresponding pins and detents.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Complete Cleaning, Lubricating the Upper and Lower Receivers, p.29

steps.title: Interval — 1,500 to 2,000 rounds; this rifle likes oil
steps.action: Hi-Point's complete-clean interval is every 1,500 to 2,000 rounds, or any time the rifle gets wet or is exposed to weather. Unlike Hi-Point's blowback guns, the HP-15 is built to run with a generous amount of lubrication. If you overdo it, expect a burst of oil in the first few shots while the rifle throws off the excess — that is not a fault.
steps.quote: Your Hi-Point HP-15 is designed to operate properly with a generous amount of lubrication.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Complete Cleaning, p.30

steps.title: Inspect before it goes back together
steps.action: Before assembly, inspect the barrel for lead build-up, bulges, cracks or obstructions, and the receivers and bolt for corrosion or visible damage. A barrel with any of those does not go back into service: the maker replaces it.
steps.quote: Do not use a cracked, bulged or obstructed barrel. Contact Strassell’s Machine, Inc. for instructions on having it replaced.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Complete Cleaning, p.30

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the lower receiver, the upper receiver with its barrel, the charging handle, the bolt carrier, the bolt, the cam pin, the firing pin, the firing pin retaining pin, and the magazine. That is the whole of the disassembly Hi-Point publishes for the HP-15. The book stops there, and its warranty is void if the rifle is taken further.
steps.prose: The warranty clause refers to 'Chapter 9'; the disassembly itself is the book's Chapter 8, which this guide follows to its last step.
steps.quote: Your Hi-Point HP-15 is disassembled beyond the instructions in Chapter 9 of the Instruction Manual.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL HP-15 5.56X45/.223REM .300BLK — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 15, Limited Lifetime Warranty, p.43

deepAbsentReason: The book's disassembly (Chapter 8, pp.23-26) ends with the bolt pulled forward out of the bolt carrier (step 13, p.26) and publishes no further procedure: the extractor, ejector, gas rings, gas key and every lower-receiver part appear only in the parts lists (pp.38-41), and Chapter 9 cleans and lubricates the lower receiver and the buffer assembled (p.29). The warranty is void if the HP-15 "is disassembled beyond the instructions in Chapter 9 of the Instruction Manual" (p.43). There is nothing deeper in the book to author.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Solvent-wet patch through the barrel from the CHAMBER end, several times, with a cleaning rod
Solvent-wet bristle brush back and forth from the chamber end
Oiled patch through once and examined; repeat brush and patch until it comes out clean
Before firing, clean dry patches from the chamber end until no oil comes out — skip only if it is going into storage
Nylon brush and solvent over the outside of the barrel, then wipe dry
Jacketed, commercially made ammunition only

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Firing pin: a light coat of CLP
Carrier: inner and outer surfaces, the cam pin area and the rails that ride in the upper
Bolt: the cam pin area and the gas rings; only a light touch on the extractor and its pin
Charging handle: lubricate the handle, its latch and spring
Carrier key: dry the inside with a swab or pipe cleaner, then ONE drop of CLP

cleaning.name: UPPER & LOWER RECEIVERS
tasks: Upper: lightly oil the inside, the bore and chamber, the outside of the barrel and under the handguard
Oil in and around the barrel's locking lugs; oil the forward assist and check it works
Lower: lubricate the trigger, hammer, safety, bolt catch and magazine release with their pins and detents
Lubricate the takedown pins and their detents
Lightly oil the buffer and buffer spring inside the buffer tube
Lint-free cloth and a little lubricant over the outside of both receivers, the handguard, exposed barrel, buffer tube and inside the magazine well
Do not pull the trigger while the upper is off — the hammer can crack the lower

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Inspect the magazine for dirt or visible damage
Wipe the outside and the feed lips with a patch slightly dampened with solvent or CLP, until the patch stays clean
Check the follower and feed lips are not damaged
Press the follower down with a fingertip and release — it must spring back up and not catch

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION & INSPECTION
tasks: Complete clean every 1,500-2,000 rounds, or any time the rifle gets wet
This rifle runs with generous lubrication; excess shows as a burst of oil in the first few shots
Inspect the barrel for lead build-up, bulges, cracks or obstructions
Inspect the receivers and bolt for corrosion or visible damage
Do not use a cracked, bulged or obstructed barrel — contact Strassell's Machine, Inc.

reassembly: Bolt into the front of the carrier with the extractor facing away from you.
Press the bolt all the way in and turn it to line up the cam pin hole with the carrier; drop the cam pin in, turn it 90 degrees, then pull the bolt forward.
Firing pin all the way into the back of the carrier.
Firing pin retaining pin in from LEFT to RIGHT, behind the firing pin's collar, pressed in until flush with the side of the carrier.
Note the ears on the charging handle; line them up with the notch in the upper and insert the handle.
Bolt carrier into the upper, using the slot in the charging handle as a guide; press it forward — the charging handle moves with it — until the bolt locks into the barrel in battery.
Never pull the trigger with the upper off.
Line the upper up on the lower at the front takedown pin and pivot it down (or set it straight down in line), then press in the front takedown pin, then the rear.
Pull the charging handle fully back and release it; the bolt must return fully forward into battery.
fncheck: With the rifle confirmed empty, chamber and magazine, run Hi-Point's function check. Insert an empty magazine and feel it lock in. Selector on FIRE, pull the charging handle fully back and release: the bolt must lock open on the hold-open. Press the magazine release and check the magazine drops out easily, then leave it out. Pull the charging handle fully back and release it and the bolt must run fully forward; with your finger off the trigger, cycle it several times to confirm it moves freely. Then, muzzle in a safe direction: selector on SAFE, the trigger must not release the hammer, with the magazine out and again with an empty magazine in; selector on FIRE, the trigger must release it. The selector only goes to SAFE with the hammer cocked, so charge the rifle before each SAFE test.
